tone_statements.citation: Pache, Matthias J. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan historical linguistics. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. 715 pp. (section 2.3.1 'Atanques', pp. 246-248).
tone_statements.quote: Some vowels bear an acute accent such as <chú> 'calabash' (Celedón 1892a: 592). It is not clear what this diacritic refers to, it may be stress or tone. As to the sounds referred to by <ü> and <ö>, Celedón (ibid.) informs the reader that they are pronounced as in German.
tone_statements.locator: p. 247, section 2.3.1.1.1 'Atanques vowels and suprasegmental features' (section starts p. 246)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference records for kank1244 (Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Ortíz Ricaurte 2000 [a Kogui sketch, mis-tagged], de Wavrin & Trillos 1998, Lehmann 1920, Celedón 1892, Celedón 1886, Reclus 1861)

sources.note: Nothing; toponymy. Useful only as a summary of Trillos Amaya 1998 (106-item comparison of Celedón/Bolinder/Castro Trespalacios data with Damana and Kogui) and as a bibliography lead.

sources.citation: Jackson, Robert T. 1995. Fonología comparativa de los idiomas chibchas de la Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. Boletín Museo del Oro 38-39: 57-69.
sources.note: Nothing on stress in any language; the 'Kankuama' section (pp. 66-67) only places Kankuamo/Atánquez next to Dámana on the basis of shared sound changes in Celedón's data ('los datos publicados sobre el kankuama (atánquez) son muy pocos y fueron transcritos fonéticamente').

sources.citation: Celedón, Rafael. 1892. Vocabulario de la lengua Atanques. In: Congrès International des Américanistes, compte-rendu de la huitième session tenue à Paris en 1890, 591-599. Paris: Ernest Leroux.
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonological prose is a 5-line pronunciation key on p. 591 ('Las reglas de pronunciacion son las siguientes: Vocales: ö, ü como en aleman; Consonantes: ch como en castellano, sh en inglés, h la jota castellana, j en francés'); pp. 591-599 are a Spanish-Atanques wordlist that marks an acute accent on most polysyllables (e.g. chakúku 'cabeza', uráka 'casa', guanoríke 'abajo', dusín 'conchita', dúmischi 'garganta') but states no rule.
sources.venue: Congrès International des Américanistes, compte-rendu de la huitième session tenue à Paris en 1890

sources.citation: Celedón, Rafael. 1886. Gramática de la lengua Kóggaba con vocabularios y catecismos (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine X). Paris: Maisonneuve. [Glottolog also lists the 1986 reprint of the Introducción in Boletín Museo del Oro 17: 9-30]
sources.note: Nothing for Atanques; the Introducción (p. xviii) only says 'En Atánquez se habla una lengua muy semejante á la Guamaka' and predicts its loss within two generations. (The grammar's accent remarks concern Kogui, not Atanques.)

sources.citation: Pache, Matthias J. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan historical linguistics. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. 715 pp. (section 2.3.1 'Atanques', pp. 246-248).
sources.quote: Some vowels bear an acute accent such as <chú> 'calabash' (Celedón 1892a: 592). It is not clear what this diacritic refers to, it may be stress or tone. As to the sounds referred to by <ü> and <ö>, Celedón (ibid.) informs the reader that they are pronounced as in German.
sources.locator: p. 247, section 2.3.1.1.1 'Atanques vowels and suprasegmental features' (section starts p. 246)
sources.note: The subsection 'Atanques vowels and suprasegmental features' (pp. 246-247) says the only evidence is Celedón's acute accent on some vowels and that it is unclear whether the diacritic marks stress or tone; footnote 22 notes stress/tone-vowel interaction in Cabécar and Ika as the reason suprasegmentals are treated under vowels. No tone inventory can be given for this extinct wordlist language.

sources.citation: Vargas Quintero, Johan David. 2023. Aspectos relevantes en la búsqueda de la identidad lingüística del pueblo kankuamo en la comunidad de Atánquez (resguardo indígena kankuamo, Colombia). Tesis de Maestría en Lingüística, Universidad de Sonora, Hermosillo. 147 pp.

tone.quote: Sin embargo, en cuanto a su sistema fonético-fonológico, del cual no hay un registro en la lengua, está sujeto a un estudio más detallado y que apuntale a la disciplina de la lingüística encargada de este.
tone.locator: p. 17, Capítulo 2, end of the section comparing Kankuamo with Damana/Ika/Kogui; interview remark on 'subir tonos' at p. 92
tone.translation: However, as for its phonetic-phonological system, of which there is no record in the language, it remains subject to a more detailed study supported by the branch of linguistics in charge of it.
